title: Cylindrical object
spec: Create a new coordinate system by setting the Euler angles to negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and set the translation vector to zero, zero, and zero. Draw the first two-dimensional sketch by creating a single face and within this face, create a single loop. Inside this loop, draw a circle centered at coordinates zero point zero five four five, zero point zero five four five, with a radius of zero point zero five four five. Apply a scaling factor of zero point one zero nine one to the entire two-dimensional sketch. Transform the two-dimensional sketch into three dimensions by rotating it using the Euler angles negative ninety degrees, zero degrees, and negative ninety degrees, and translate it using the translation vector zero, zero, and zero. Extrude the two-dimensional sketch along the normal by zero point seven five units without extruding in the opposite direction, ensuring that the operation creates a new solid body. The final cylindrical object will have a length of zero point one zero nine one units, a width of zero point one zero nine one units, and a height of zero point seven five units.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the circle
circle = r.center(0.0545, 0.0545).circle(0.0545)

# Extrude the circle to create a cylinder
cylinder = circle.extrude(0.75)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90, 0, -90) and the translation vector is (0, 0, 0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the cylinder 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
cylinder = cylinder.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model
r = cylinder

# Create the sketch with the circle

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
extrude_depth = 0.75

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90, 0, -90) and the translation vector is (0, 0, 0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the cylinder 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis

lanes.label: Cadabra 4B (ours) · 1 sample

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the circle for the sketch
circle_center = (0.0545, 0.0545)
circle_radius = 0.0545

# Create the sketch on the XY plane
r = r.center(*circle_center).circle(circle_radius)

# Extrude the sketch to create the cylinder
extrude_depth = 0.75
r = r.extrude(extrude_depth)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90, 0, -90) and the translation vector is (0, 0, 0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the cylinder 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90).rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)
